questions.q: What happens to a local variable once its function finishes running?
options: It no longer exists — it was created and destroyed within the function's scope
It becomes a global variable automatically
It keeps its value and can be read from outside the function
It resets to None but stays accessible
questions.explain: Local variables exist only while their function is running.

questions.q: Why is modifying a global variable from inside a function generally discouraged?
options: It makes the function's behavior depend on and silently change state outside itself, making it harder to test and reason about
Python does not allow it syntactically
It always causes a program to crash
Global variables cannot hold numeric values
questions.explain: Returning a value and letting the caller manage state is a more predictable, testable pattern.

questions.q: What does return False, "invalid quantity" actually return?
options: A tuple: (False, "invalid quantity")
Two separate return statements
Only the string, discarding the boolean
A dictionary with two keys
questions.explain: Separating return values with a comma packs them into a tuple.

questions.q: What does is_valid, reason = validate_order(row) do?
options: Unpacks the two-item tuple returned by the function into two separate variables
Calls the function twice
Raises an error because a function can't return two things
Creates a new function named is_valid
questions.explain: Unpacking assigns each value in the returned tuple to its own variable in one line.

questions.q: Why is a validate_order function that returns (is_valid, reason) more useful than one that returns only True or False?
options: It tells the caller why a row was rejected, not just whether it was, which is useful for logging later
It runs faster than a function returning a single value
It avoids needing an if statement entirely
There is no real benefit; returning two values is purely stylistic
questions.explain: Returning a reason alongside the validity flag gives the caller actionable detail about a rejection.
